section_1.title: The Slice: From 3D to 2D
section_1.content: Introduce the prerequisite concept of a 'conic section' by intersecting a double cone with a plane. Focus on the visual formation of an ellipse and define it by its locus: the set of points where the sum of distances to two foci is constant.
section_1.example: Imagine a 'Geometric Chef' slicing a perfectly conical carrot at an angle with a laser; the resulting cross-section is a smooth, purple-edged ellipse.

section_2.title: The Magic Spheres Appear
section_2.content: Introduce the Dandelin Spheres: two spheres placed inside the cone, one above the plane and one below. Each sphere is 'inscribed' so it is tangent to the cone (along a circle) and tangent to the cutting plane at exactly one point ($F_1$ and $F_2$).
section_2.example: Visualize two glowing soap bubbles inflating inside a glass cone until they are snugly trapped by a tilted glass shelf (the plane).

section_3.title: Prerequisite: The Ice Cream Cone Lemma
section_3.content: Establish the critical geometric tool: tangents from a single point to a sphere are equal in length. This is essential for the transition to the formal proof.
section_3.example: An ant standing at a point $P$ outside a sphere measures the distance to the 'horizon' of the sphere; no matter which direction it looks, the distance to the touch-point is identical.

section_4.title: The Visual Proof: Linking Segments
section_4.content: Pick an arbitrary point $P$ on the ellipse. Draw segments $PF_1$ and $PF_2$. Show that $PF_1$ is equal to the segment along the cone's surface to the upper circle of contact ($PA$), and $PF_2$ is equal to the segment to the lower circle ($PB$).
section_4.example: Use color-coded neon lines: $PF_1$ (blue) and $PF_2$ (red) magically 'fold' onto the surface of the cone to form a single straight line segment $AB$ along the slant height.

section_5.title: The Constant Sum
section_5.content: Demonstrate that the total length $PF_1 + PF_2$ is always equal to the distance $AB$ along the cone's slant height between the two contact circles. Since the circles are fixed, this distance is constant regardless of where $P$ is moved.
section_5.example: A 'Space Navigator' notices that as their ship travels the elliptical orbit ($P$), the combined length of the two fuel tethers ($PF_1$ and $PF_2$) remains as rigid as a fixed metal rod.

section_6.title: Universal Application: Parabolas and Hyperbolas
section_6.content: Briefly extend the logic: explain that by tilting the plane further, we interact with the spheres differently to create parabolas or hyperbolas, proving all conic sections share this spherical harmony.
section_6.example: The 'Geometric Chef' tilts the laser slice more steeply; the soap bubbles shift, and the ellipse 'snaps' into an open parabola, like a spotlight hitting a stage floor.

section_1.title: The Slice: From 3D to 2D
lecture_lines: A conic section forms where a plane slices a cone.
Tilting the plane creates different geometric curves.
An ellipse is defined by a constant distance sum.
animations: Draw a white triangle (#FFFFFF) representing a cone and a green line (#00FF00) representing a cutting plane.
Animate a purple ellipse (#800080) appearing at the intersection area between the cone and plane.
Highlight two yellow points F1 and F2 (#FFFF00) on the plane to indicate future foci.

section_2.title: The Magic Spheres Appear
lecture_lines: Place two spheres inside the cone, above and below.
Inflate them until they touch the cone's surface.
Each sphere also touches the tilted cutting plane.
They are tangent to the plane at points $F_1, F_2$.
These tangent points are the foci of our ellipse.
animations: Show the cone and plane; draw a small yellow circle (#FFFF00) tangent to both cone walls and the plane.
Draw a larger cyan circle (#0000FF) below the plane, tangent to both cone walls and the plane.
Mark and label the tangency points on the plane as F1 (#FFFF00) and F2 (#0000FF).

section_3.title: Prerequisite: The Ice Cream Cone Lemma
lecture_lines: Tangents from a point to a sphere are equal.
This is known as the "Ice Cream Cone Lemma."
Distances from the vertex to the contact circle match.
animations: Draw a white circle (#FFFFFF) representing a sphere and a red point P (#FF0000) outside it.
Draw two tangent segments from P to the circle's boundary.
Flash the two segments and add small white equality marks (#FFFFFF) to show they have equal length.

section_4.title: The Visual Proof: Linking Segments
lecture_lines: Pick any point $P$ on the elliptical slice.
Connect $P$ to the foci $F_1$ and $F_2$.
$PF_1$ equals the distance to the upper contact circle.
$PF_2$ equals the distance to the lower contact circle.
These segments align along the cone's slant height.
animations: Display the cone, plane, and spheres with a red point P (#FF0000) on the ellipse.
Draw a blue segment (#0000FF) connecting point P to focus F1.
Draw a blue segment from P along the cone's slant to the upper contact circle, labeled A.
Draw an orange-red segment (#FF4500) connecting point P to focus F2.
Draw an orange-red segment from P along the cone's slant to the lower contact circle, labeled B.

section_5.title: The Constant Sum
lecture_lines: The sum $PF_1 + PF_2$ equals the total slant distance.
This distance $AB$ connects the two fixed circles.
The length $AB$ remains constant as point $P$ moves.
Thus, the sum of distances to foci is constant.
The Dandelin spheres prove this curve is an ellipse.
animations: Highlight segments PF1 and PA in blue (#0000FF) and PF2 and PB in orange-red (#FF4500).
Animate PF1 rotating onto PA and PF2 rotating onto PB to show equality.
Highlight the combined slant segment AB (#00FF00) connecting the two spheres' contact circles.
Display the sum PF1 + PF2 = AB in white text (#FFFFFF) at the top.
Slide point P along the ellipse while the total length AB remains constant.

section_6.title: Universal Application: Parabolas and Hyperbolas
lecture_lines: Tilting the plane further changes the intersection's shape.
Spheres still reveal the logic of parabolas and hyperbolas.
Geometry and symmetry unite all conic sections.
animations: Show the initial ellipse and green cutting plane (#00FF00).
Tilt the plane until it is parallel to the cone's slant, changing the curve to an orange parabola (#FFA500).
Tilt the plane further to intersect a double cone, forming two pink hyperbola branches (#FFC0CB).

1. Show the cone, plane, spheres, and a point P on the ellipse.

storyboard.title: The Constant Sum
lecture_lines: The sum $PF_1 + PF_2$ equals the total slant distance.
This distance $AB$ connects the two fixed circles.
The length $AB$ remains constant as point $P$ moves.
Thus, the sum of distances to foci is constant.

                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Ice Cream Cone Lemma", [
            "- Tangents from a point to a sphere are equal.",
            "- This is known as the \"Ice Cream Cone Lemma.\"",
            "- Distances from the vertex to the contact circle match."
        ])
        
        # Initial lecture colors - start dimmed for progressive highlight
        self.lecture.set_color(GRAY)
        
        # Visual Element Colors
        sphere_color = WHITE
        point_p_color = RED
        tangent_color = WHITE
        mark_color = WHITE
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # Create a circle representing the sphere (2D projection)
        sphere = Circle(radius=1.2, color=sphere_color)
        self.place_in_area(sphere, 'C3', 'E5')
        
        # Create point P outside the sphere
        p_dot = Dot(color=point_p_color)
        self.place_at_grid(p_dot, 'D1')
        p_label = MathTex("P", color=point_p_color).next_to(p_dot, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        # Geometry setup
        c = sphere.get_center()
        p = p_dot.get_center()
        r = sphere.radius
        cp_vec = p - c
        dist_cp = np.linalg.norm(cp_vec)
        
        # Calculate tangent points on the circle
        # In 2D, the angle of the tangent points relative to center is angle(P-C) +/- arccos(r/d)
        angle_cp = np.arctan2(cp_vec[1], cp_vec[0])
        angle_ct = np.arccos(r / dist_cp)
        
        t1_pos = c + r * np.array([np.cos(angle_cp + angle_ct), np.sin(angle_cp + angle_ct), 0])
        t2_pos = c + r * np.array([np.cos(angle_cp - angle_ct), np.sin(angle_cp - angle_ct), 0])
        
        l1 = Line(p, t1_pos, color=tangent_color)
        l2 = Line(p, t2_pos, color=tangent_color)
        
        self.play(Create(sphere), FadeIn(p_dot), Write(p_label))
        self.play(Create(l1), Create(l2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(RED))
        
        # Visualize the vertex of the "cone"
        self.play(Indicate(p_dot, color=RED), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # Flash both tangent segments to emphasize their equal lengths
        self.play(
            Flash(l1, color=WHITE, line_length=0.3, flash_radius=0.5),
            Flash(l2, color=WHITE, line_length=0.3, flash_radius=0.5)
        )
        
        # Equality markers (ticks)
        def create_tick(line):
            mid = line.get_center()
            vec = line.get_unit_vector()
            # Calculate a normal vector for the tick
            normal = np.array([-vec[1], vec[0], 0])
            return Line(mid - 0.12 * normal, mid + 0.12 * normal, color=mark_color, stroke_width=3)

        tick1 = create_tick(l1)
        tick2 = create_tick(l2)
        
        self.play(Create(tick1), Create(tick2))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup
        title_str = "The Constant Sum"
        lines_str = [
            "The sum PF1 + PF2 equals the total slant distance.",
            "This distance AB connects the two fixed circles.",
            "The length AB remains constant as point P moves.",
            "Thus, the sum of distances to foci is constant.",
            "The Dandelin spheres prove this curve is an ellipse."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_str, lines_str)

        # Colors
        COLOR_PF1 = "#0000FF" # Blue
        COLOR_PF2 = "#FF4500" # Orange-red
        COLOR_AB = "#00FF00"  # Green
        COLOR_TEXT = "#FFFFFF"

        # Points
        f1_pos = self.grid["D2"] + RIGHT * 0.2
        f2_pos = self.grid["D5"] + LEFT * 0.2
        a_pos = self.grid["C3"]
        b_pos = self.grid["E5"]
        
        # Fixed distance AB length
        ab_len = np.linalg.norm(b_pos - a_pos)
        
        # P's path - Ellipse logic
        # Sum of distances to foci = constant = ab_len
        center_ellipse = (f1_pos + f2_pos) / 2
        c_dist = np.linalg.norm(f1_pos - center_ellipse)
        a_semi = ab_len / 2
        b_semi = np.sqrt(max(a_semi**2 - c_dist**2, 0.1)) # semi-minor axis
        
        ellipse_path = Ellipse(width=2*a_semi, height=2*b_semi, color=GRAY, stroke_opacity=0.3).move_to(center_ellipse)
        
        # Initial P
        dot_p = Dot(ellipse_path.point_from_proportion(0), color=WHITE)
        label_p = MathTex("P", font_size=24).next_to(dot_p, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        dot_f1 = Dot(f1_pos, color=COLOR_PF1)
        label_f1 = MathTex("F_1", font_size=24, color=COLOR_PF1).next_to(dot_f1, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        dot_f2 = Dot(f2_pos, color=COLOR_PF2)
        label_f2 = MathTex("F_2", font_size=24, color=COLOR_PF2).next_to(dot_f2, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        dot_a = Dot(a_pos, color=COLOR_PF1)
        label_a = MathTex("A", font_size=24, color=COLOR_PF1).next_to(dot_a, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        dot_b = Dot(b_pos, color=COLOR_PF2)
        label_b = MathTex("B", font_size=24, color=COLOR_PF2).next_to(dot_b, RIGHT, buff=0.1)

        # Segments
        line_pf1 = Line(dot_p.get_center(), f1_pos, color=COLOR_PF1)
        line_pf2 = Line(dot_p.get_center(), f2_pos, color=COLOR_PF2)
        
        # Components of AB segment (initially placeholders)
        line_pa = Line(a_pos, a_pos, color=COLOR_PF1, stroke_width=8)
        line_pb = Line(b_pos, b_pos, color=COLOR_PF2, stroke_width=8)
        line_ab = Line(a_pos, b_pos, color=COLOR_AB, stroke_width=4)

        formula = MathTex("PF_1 + PF_2 = AB", font_size=32, color=COLOR_TEXT)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B4")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.add(dot_p, label_p, dot_f1, label_f1, dot_f2, label_f2, dot_a, label_a, dot_b, label_b)
        self.play(Create(line_pf1), Create(line_pf2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Calculate target segments on AB for initial P
        p_curr = dot_p.get_center()
        d1 = np.linalg.norm(p_curr - f1_pos)
        d2 = np.linalg.norm(p_curr - f2_pos)
        dir_ab = (b_pos - a_pos) / ab_len
        
        target_pa = Line(a_pos, a_pos + dir_ab * d1, color=COLOR_PF1, stroke_width=8)
        target_pb = Line(b_pos, b_pos - dir_ab * d2, color=COLOR_PF2, stroke_width=8)
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(line_pf1.copy(), target_pa),
            ReplacementTransform(line_pf2.copy(), target_pb),
            run_time=2
        )
        line_pa.become(target_pa)
        line_pb.become(target_pb)
        self.add(line_pa, line_pb)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(line_ab))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        self.play(Create(ellipse_path))
        
        p_tracker = ValueTracker(0)

        # Define Updaters
        def update_p_obj(m):
            m.move_to(ellipse_path.point_from_proportion(p_tracker.get_value() % 1.0))
            
        def update_label_p_obj(m):
            m.next_to(dot_p, UP, buff=0.1)
            
        def update_line_pf1_obj(m):
            m.set_points_as_corners([dot_p.get_center(), f1_pos])
            
        def update_line_pf2_obj(m):
            m.set_points_as_corners([dot_p.get_center(), f2_pos])

        def update_line_pa_obj(m):
            dist = np.linalg.norm(dot_p.get_center() - f1_pos)
            m.set_points_as_corners([a_pos, a_pos + dir_ab * dist])

        def update_line_pb_obj(m):
            dist = np.linalg.norm(dot_p.get_center() - f2_pos)
            m.set_points_as_corners([b_pos, b_pos - dir_ab * dist])

        # Attach Updaters
        dot_p.add_updater(update_p_obj)
        label_p.add_updater(update_label_p_obj)
        line_pf1.add_updater(update_line_pf1_obj)
        line_pf2.add_updater(update_line_pf2_obj)
        line_pa.add_updater(update_line_pa_obj)
        line_pb.add_updater(update_line_pb_obj)
        
        self.play(p_tracker.animate.set_value(1), run_time=6, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Cleanup updaters for static final frame
        dot_p.clear_updaters()
        label_p.clear_updaters()
        line_pf1.clear_updaters()
        line_pf2.clear_updaters()
        line_pa.clear_updaters()
        line_pb.clear_updaters()
        
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: The Constant Sum
outline.content: Demonstrate that the total length $PF_1 + PF_2$ is always equal to the distance $AB$ along the cone's slant height between the two contact circles. Since the circles are fixed, this distance is constant regardless of where $P$ is moved.
outline.example: A 'Space Navigator' notices that as their ship travels the elliptical orbit ($P$), the combined length of the two fuel tethers ($PF_1$ and $PF_2$) remains as rigid as a fixed metal rod.

storyboard.title: The Constant Sum
lecture_lines: The sum $PF_1 + PF_2$ equals the total slant distance.
This distance $AB$ connects the two fixed circles.
The length $AB$ remains constant as point $P$ moves.
Thus, the sum of distances to foci is constant.
The Dandelin spheres prove this curve is an ellipse.
animations: Highlight segments PF1 and PA in blue (#0000FF) and PF2 and PB in orange-red (#FF4500).
Animate PF1 rotating onto PA and PF2 rotating onto PB to show equality.
Highlight the combined slant segment AB (#00FF00) connecting the two spheres' [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg] contact circles.
Display the sum PF1 + PF2 = AB in white text (#FFFFFF) at the top.
Slide point P along the ellipse while the total length AB remains constant.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup
        title_str = "The Constant Sum"
        lines_str = [
            "The sum PF1 + PF2 equals the total slant distance.",
            "This distance AB connects the two fixed circles.",
            "The length AB remains constant as point P moves.",
            "Thus, the sum of distances to foci is constant.",
            "The Dandelin spheres prove this curve is an ellipse."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_str, lines_str)

        # Colors
        COLOR_PF1 = "#0000FF" # Blue
        COLOR_PF2 = "#FF4500" # Orange-red
        COLOR_AB = "#00FF00"  # Green
        COLOR_TEXT = "#FFFFFF"

        # Points
        f1_pos = self.grid["D2"] + RIGHT * 0.2
        f2_pos = self.grid["D5"] + LEFT * 0.2
        a_pos = self.grid["C3"]
        b_pos = self.grid["E5"]
        
        # Fixed distance AB length
        ab_len = np.linalg.norm(b_pos - a_pos)
        
        # P's path - Ellipse logic
        # Sum of distances to foci = constant = ab_len
        center_ellipse = (f1_pos + f2_pos) / 2
        c_dist = np.linalg.norm(f1_pos - center_ellipse)
        a_semi = ab_len / 2
        b_semi = np.sqrt(max(a_semi**2 - c_dist**2, 0.1)) # semi-minor axis
        
        ellipse_path = Ellipse(width=2*a_semi, height=2*b_semi, color=GRAY, stroke_opacity=0.3).move_to(center_ellipse)
        
        # Initial P
        dot_p = Dot(ellipse_path.point_from_proportion(0), color=WHITE)
        label_p = MathTex("P", font_size=24).next_to(dot_p, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        dot_f1 = Dot(f1_pos, color=COLOR_PF1)
        label_f1 = MathTex("F_1", font_size=24, color=COLOR_PF1).next_to(dot_f1, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        dot_f2 = Dot(f2_pos, color=COLOR_PF2)
        label_f2 = MathTex("F_2", font_size=24, color=COLOR_PF2).next_to(dot_f2, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        dot_a = Dot(a_pos, color=COLOR_PF1)
        label_a = MathTex("A", font_size=24, color=COLOR_PF1).next_to(dot_a, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        dot_b = Dot(b_pos, color=COLOR_PF2)
        label_b = MathTex("B", font_size=24, color=COLOR_PF2).next_to(dot_b, RIGHT, buff=0.1)

        # Segments
        line_pf1 = Line(dot_p.get_center(), f1_pos, color=COLOR_PF1)
        line_pf2 = Line(dot_p.get_center(), f2_pos, color=COLOR_PF2)
        
        # Components of AB segment (initially placeholders)
        line_pa = Line(a_pos, a_pos, color=COLOR_PF1, stroke_width=8)
        line_pb = Line(b_pos, b_pos, color=COLOR_PF2, stroke_width=8)
        line_ab = Line(a_pos, b_pos, color=COLOR_AB, stroke_width=4)

        formula = MathTex("PF_1 + PF_2 = AB", font_size=32, color=COLOR_TEXT)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B4")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.add(dot_p, label_p, dot_f1, label_f1, dot_f2, label_f2, dot_a, label_a, dot_b, label_b)
        self.play(Create(line_pf1), Create(line_pf2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Calculate target segments on AB for initial P
        p_curr = dot_p.get_center()
        d1 = np.linalg.norm(p_curr - f1_pos)
        d2 = np.linalg.norm(p_curr - f2_pos)
        dir_ab = (b_pos - a_pos) / ab_len
        
        target_pa = Line(a_pos, a_pos + dir_ab * d1, color=COLOR_PF1, stroke_width=8)
        target_pb = Line(b_pos, b_pos - dir_ab * d2, color=COLOR_PF2, stroke_width=8)
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(line_pf1.copy(), target_pa),
            ReplacementTransform(line_pf2.copy(), target_pb),
            run_time=2
        )
        line_pa.become(target_pa)
        line_pb.become(target_pb)
        self.add(line_pa, line_pb)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(line_ab))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        self.play(Create(ellipse_path))
        
        p_tracker = ValueTracker(0)

        # Define Updaters
        def update_p_obj(m):
            m.move_to(ellipse_path.point_from_proportion(p_tracker.get_value() % 1.0))
            
        def update_label_p_obj(m):
            m.next_to(dot_p, UP, buff=0.1)
            
        def update_line_pf1_obj(m):
            m.set_points_as_corners([dot_p.get_center(), f1_pos])
            
        def update_line_pf2_obj(m):
            m.set_points_as_corners([dot_p.get_center(), f2_pos])

        def update_line_pa_obj(m):
            dist = np.linalg.norm(dot_p.get_center() - f1_pos)
            m.set_points_as_corners([a_pos, a_pos + dir_ab * dist])

        def update_line_pb_obj(m):
            dist = np.linalg.norm(dot_p.get_center() - f2_pos)
            m.set_points_as_corners([b_pos, b_pos - dir_ab * dist])

        # Attach Updaters
        dot_p.add_updater(update_p_obj)
        label_p.add_updater(update_label_p_obj)
        line_pf1.add_updater(update_line_pf1_obj)
        line_pf2.add_updater(update_line_pf2_obj)
        line_pa.add_updater(update_line_pa_obj)
        line_pb.add_updater(update_line_pb_obj)
        
        self.play(p_tracker.animate.set_value(1), run_time=6, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Cleanup updaters for static final frame
        dot_p.clear_updaters()
        label_p.clear_updaters()
        line_pf1.clear_updaters()
        line_pf2.clear_updaters()
        line_pa.clear_updaters()
        line_pb.clear_updaters()
        
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup
        title_str = "The Constant Sum"
        lines_str = [
            "The sum PF1 + PF2 equals the total slant distance.",
            "This distance AB connects the two fixed circles.",
            "The length AB remains constant as point P moves.",
            "Thus, the sum of distances to foci is constant.",
            "The Dandelin spheres prove this curve is an ellipse."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_str, lines_str)

        # Colors
        COLOR_PF1 = "#0000FF" # Blue
        COLOR_PF2 = "#FF4500" # Orange-red
        COLOR_AB = "#00FF00"  # Green
        COLOR_TEXT = "#FFFFFF"

        # Assets
        sphere_asset_path = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg"

        # Points
        f1_pos = self.grid["D2"] + RIGHT * 0.2
        f2_pos = self.grid["D5"] + LEFT * 0.2
        a_pos = self.grid["C3"]
        b_pos = self.grid["E5"]
        
        # Fixed distance AB length
        ab_len = np.linalg.norm(b_pos - a_pos)
        
        # P's path - Ellipse logic
        # Sum of distances to foci = constant = ab_len
        center_ellipse = (f1_pos + f2_pos) / 2
        c_dist = np.linalg.norm(f1_pos - center_ellipse)
        a_semi = ab_len / 2

        ellipse_path = Ellipse(width=2*a_semi, height=2*b_semi, color=GRAY, stroke_opacity=0.3).move_to(center_ellipse)

        line_pf2.add_updater(update_pf2)
        line_pa.add_updater(update_pa)

section_1.title: The Slice: From 3D to 2D
section_1.content: Introduce the prerequisite concept of a 'conic section' by intersecting a double cone with a plane. Focus on the visual formation of an ellipse and define it by its locus: the set of points where the sum of distances to two foci is constant.
section_1.example: Imagine a 'Geometric Chef' slicing a perfectly conical carrot at an angle with a laser; the resulting cross-section is a smooth, purple-edged ellipse.

section_2.title: The Magic Spheres Appear
section_2.content: Introduce the Dandelin Spheres: two spheres placed inside the cone, one above the plane and one below. Each sphere is 'inscribed' so it is tangent to the cone (along a circle) and tangent to the cutting plane at exactly one point ($F_1$ and $F_2$).
section_2.example: Visualize two glowing soap bubbles inflating inside a glass cone until they are snugly trapped by a tilted glass shelf (the plane).

section_3.title: Prerequisite: The Ice Cream Cone Lemma
section_3.content: Establish the critical geometric tool: tangents from a single point to a sphere are equal in length. This is essential for the transition to the formal proof.
section_3.example: An ant standing at a point $P$ outside a sphere measures the distance to the 'horizon' of the sphere; no matter which direction it looks, the distance to the touch-point is identical.

section_4.title: The Visual Proof: Linking Segments
section_4.content: Pick an arbitrary point $P$ on the ellipse. Draw segments $PF_1$ and $PF_2$. Show that $PF_1$ is equal to the segment along the cone's surface to the upper circle of contact ($PA$), and $PF_2$ is equal to the segment to the lower circle ($PB$).
section_4.example: Use color-coded neon lines: $PF_1$ (blue) and $PF_2$ (red) magically 'fold' onto the surface of the cone to form a single straight line segment $AB$ along the slant height.

section_5.title: The Constant Sum
section_5.content: Demonstrate that the total length $PF_1 + PF_2$ is always equal to the distance $AB$ along the cone's slant height between the two contact circles. Since the circles are fixed, this distance is constant regardless of where $P$ is moved.
section_5.example: A 'Space Navigator' notices that as their ship travels the elliptical orbit ($P$), the combined length of the two fuel tethers ($PF_1$ and $PF_2$) remains as rigid as a fixed metal rod.

section_6.title: Universal Application: Parabolas and Hyperbolas
section_6.content: Briefly extend the logic: explain that by tilting the plane further, we interact with the spheres differently to create parabolas or hyperbolas, proving all conic sections share this spherical harmony.
section_6.example: The 'Geometric Chef' tilts the laser slice more steeply; the soap bubbles shift, and the ellipse 'snaps' into an open parabola, like a spotlight hitting a stage floor.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize title and lecture lines
        title_text = "The Slice: From 3D to 2D"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- A conic section forms where a plane slices a cone.",
            "- Tilting the plane creates different geometric curves.",
            "- An ellipse is defined by a constant distance sum."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight first line in WHITE
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # Draw a white triangle representing a cone
        cone = Triangle(color=WHITE).scale(1.5)
        self.place_in_area(cone, "A3", "E5", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # Draw a green line representing a cutting plane
        plane_line = Line(LEFT * 2.5, RIGHT * 2.5, color="#00FF00")
        plane_line.rotate(20 * DEGREES)
        # Position the plane so it intersects the cone
        self.place_in_area(plane_line, "C3", "D5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Create(cone), Create(plane_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Transition highlight to second line (PURPLE)
        # Note: Colors are adjusted to be distinct as requested
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#800080")
        )
        
        # Animate a purple ellipse appearing at the intersection
        ellipse = Ellipse(width=2.2, height=0.6, color="#800080")
        # Place ellipse at the intersection area
        self.place_in_area(ellipse, "C3", "D5", scale_factor=0.9)
        # Rotate ellipse to align with the plane's tilt
        ellipse.rotate(20 * DEGREES)
        
        self.play(Create(ellipse))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Transition highlight to third line (YELLOW)
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00")
        )

        f1_dot = Dot(color="#FFFF00")
        f2_dot = Dot(color="#FFFF00")
        
        # Position foci relative to the ellipse center and rotation
        ellipse_center = ellipse.get_center()
        # Rotation vector for 20 degrees
        rot_vec = np.array([np.cos(20*DEGREES), np.sin(20*DEGREES), 0])
        
        f1_dot.move_to(ellipse_center - 0.7 * rot_vec)
        f2_dot.move_to(ellipse_center + 0.7 * rot_vec)
        
        f1_label = MathTex("F_1", color="#FFFF00", font_size=24)
        f2_label = MathTex("F_2", color="#FFFF00", font_size=24)
        
        # Labels positioned near the foci
        f1_label.next_to(f1_dot, UP, buff=0.1)
        f2_label.next_to(f2_dot, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(f1_dot), FadeIn(f2_dot),
            Write(f1_label), Write(f2_label)
        )
        self.wait(3)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Ice Cream Cone Lemma", [
            "- Tangents from a point to a sphere are equal.",
            "- This is known as the \"Ice Cream Cone Lemma.\"",
            "- Distances from the vertex to the contact circle match."
        ])
        
        # Initial lecture colors - start dimmed for progressive highlight
        self.lecture.set_color(GRAY)
        
        # Visual Element Colors
        sphere_color = WHITE
        point_p_color = RED
        tangent_color = WHITE
        mark_color = WHITE
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # Create a circle representing the sphere (2D projection)
        sphere = Circle(radius=1.2, color=sphere_color)
        self.place_in_area(sphere, 'C3', 'E5')
        
        # Create point P outside the sphere
        p_dot = Dot(color=point_p_color)
        self.place_at_grid(p_dot, 'D1')
        p_label = MathTex("P", color=point_p_color).next_to(p_dot, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        # Geometry setup
        c = sphere.get_center()
        p = p_dot.get_center()
        r = sphere.radius
        cp_vec = p - c
        dist_cp = np.linalg.norm(cp_vec)
        
        # Calculate tangent points on the circle
        # In 2D, the angle of the tangent points relative to center is angle(P-C) +/- arccos(r/d)
        angle_cp = np.arctan2(cp_vec[1], cp_vec[0])
        angle_ct = np.arccos(r / dist_cp)
        
        t1_pos = c + r * np.array([np.cos(angle_cp + angle_ct), np.sin(angle_cp + angle_ct), 0])
        t2_pos = c + r * np.array([np.cos(angle_cp - angle_ct), np.sin(angle_cp - angle_ct), 0])
        
        l1 = Line(p, t1_pos, color=tangent_color)
        l2 = Line(p, t2_pos, color=tangent_color)
        
        self.play(Create(sphere), FadeIn(p_dot), Write(p_label))
        self.play(Create(l1), Create(l2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(RED))
        
        # Visualize the vertex of the "cone"
        self.play(Indicate(p_dot, color=RED), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # Flash both tangent segments to emphasize their equal lengths
        self.play(
            Flash(l1, color=WHITE, line_length=0.3, flash_radius=0.5),
            Flash(l2, color=WHITE, line_length=0.3, flash_radius=0.5)
        )
        
        # Equality markers (ticks)
        def create_tick(line):
            mid = line.get_center()
            vec = line.get_unit_vector()
            # Calculate a normal vector for the tick
            normal = np.array([-vec[1], vec[0], 0])
            return Line(mid - 0.12 * normal, mid + 0.12 * normal, color=mark_color, stroke_width=3)

        tick1 = create_tick(l1)
        tick2 = create_tick(l2)
        
        self.play(Create(tick1), Create(tick2))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Section title and lecture lines
        title_text = "The Visual Proof: Linking Segments"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Pick any point P on the elliptical slice.",
            "Connect P to the foci F1 and F2.",
            "PF1 equals the distance to the upper contact circle.",
            "PF2 equals the distance to the lower contact circle.",
            "These segments align along the cone's slant height."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_P = "#FF0000"
        COLOR_BLUE = "#0000FF"
        COLOR_ORANGE = "#FF4500"
        COLOR_CONE = GREY_C
        COLOR_SPHERE = GREY_B
        COLOR_PLANE = "#FFFFE0" # Light Yellow

        # Grid references
        g = self.grid

        # Pre-calculated geometry for visual proof consistency
        # P is the point on the ellipse
        # F1, F2 are the foci
        # A, B are points on the upper/lower contact circles along the slant height through P
        # Distances: PF1 = PA, PF2 = PB
        # Collinearity: A, P, B are on a straight line (the slant height)
        
        # Grid Coordinates (Indices start at 1):
        # P: D4 (x=1.5+3=4.5, y=2.2-3=-0.8)
        # F1: C2 (x=1.5+1=2.5, y=2.2-2=0.2) -> dist = sqrt(2^2+1^2) = sqrt(5)
        # A: B3 (x=1.5+2=3.5, y=2.2-1=1.2) -> dist = sqrt(1^2+2^2) = sqrt(5)
        # F2: E6 (x=1.5+5=6.5, y=2.2-4=-1.8) -> dist = sqrt(2^2+1^2) = sqrt(5)
        # B: F5 (x=1.5+4=5.5, y=2.2-5=-2.8) -> dist = sqrt(1^2+2^2) = sqrt(5)
        # Apex: (x=3.0, y=2.2) [Midpoint of A2 and A3]

        f1_pos = g["C2"]
        f2_pos = g["E6"]
        a_pos = g["B3"]
        b_pos = g["F5"]
        apex_pos = (g["A2"] + g["A3"]) / 2

        # Display the cone, plane, and spheres with a red point P (#FF0000) on the ellipse.
        
        # Cone sides

        slant_r = Line(apex_pos, g["F6"], color=COLOR_CONE)
        
        # Spheres
        sphere1 = Circle(radius=0.7, color=COLOR_SPHERE, stroke_opacity=0.8).set_fill(COLOR_SPHERE, opacity=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(sphere1, "B2", "B3") # Center roughly at x=3.0
        
        sphere2 = Circle(radius=1.3, color=COLOR_SPHERE, stroke_opacity=0.8).set_fill(COLOR_SPHERE, opacity=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(sphere2, "D2", "F3") # Center roughly at x=3.0
        
        # Plane line (as slice)
        plane_line = Line(g["B1"], g["F6"], color=COLOR_PLANE, stroke_width=2)
        
        # Point P
        dot_p = Dot(p_pos, color=COLOR_P)
        label_p = MathTex("P", color=COLOR_P, font_size=24).next_to(dot_p, UP, buff=0.1)

        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup
        title_str = "The Constant Sum"
        lines_str = [
            "The sum PF1 + PF2 equals the total slant distance.",
            "This distance AB connects the two fixed circles.",
            "The length AB remains constant as point P moves.",
            "Thus, the sum of distances to foci is constant.",
            "The Dandelin spheres prove this curve is an ellipse."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_str, lines_str)

        # Colors
        COLOR_PF1 = "#0000FF" # Blue
        COLOR_PF2 = "#FF4500" # Orange-red
        COLOR_AB = "#00FF00"  # Green
        COLOR_TEXT = "#FFFFFF"

        # Assets
        sphere_asset_path = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg"

        # Points
        f1_pos = self.grid["D2"] + RIGHT * 0.2
        f2_pos = self.grid["D5"] + LEFT * 0.2
        a_pos = self.grid["C3"]
        b_pos = self.grid["E5"]
        
        # Fixed distance AB length
        ab_len = np.linalg.norm(b_pos - a_pos)
        
        # P's path - Ellipse logic
        # Sum of distances to foci = constant = ab_len
        center_ellipse = (f1_pos + f2_pos) / 2
        c_dist = np.linalg.norm(f1_pos - center_ellipse)
        a_semi = ab_len / 2
        b_semi = np.sqrt(max(a_semi**2 - c_dist**2, 0.1)) # semi-minor axis
        
        ellipse_path = Ellipse(width=2*a_semi, height=2*b_semi, color=GRAY, stroke_opacity=0.3).move_to(center_ellipse)
        
        # Initial P (proportion 0.25 for a good starting angle)
        dot_p = Dot(ellipse_path.point_from_proportion(0.25), color=WHITE)
        label_p = Text("P", font_size=18).next_to(dot_p, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        dot_f1 = Dot(f1_pos, color=COLOR_PF1)
        label_f1 = Text("F1", font_size=18, color=COLOR_PF1).next_to(dot_f1, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        dot_f2 = Dot(f2_pos, color=COLOR_PF2)
        label_f2 = Text("F2", font_size=18, color=COLOR_PF2).next_to(dot_f2, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        dot_a = Dot(a_pos, color=COLOR_PF1)
        label_a = Text("A", font_size=18, color=COLOR_PF1).next_to(dot_a, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        dot_b = Dot(b_pos, color=COLOR_PF2)
        label_b = Text("B", font_size=18, color=COLOR_PF2).next_to(dot_b, RIGHT, buff=0.1)

        # Spheres at A and B
        sphere_a = SVGMobject(sphere_asset_path).scale(0.4).move_to(a_pos + UP*0.4)
        sphere_b = SVGMobject(sphere_asset_path).scale(0.6).move_to(b_pos + DOWN*0.6)

        # Segments
        line_pf1 = Line(dot_p.get_center(), f1_pos, color=COLOR_PF1)
        line_pf2 = Line(dot_p.get_center(), f2_pos, color=COLOR_PF2)
        
        # Components of AB segment
        dir_ab = (b_pos - a_pos) / ab_len
        
        # Formula using Text to avoid LaTeX issues
        formula = Text("PF1 + PF2 = AB", font_size=24, color=COLOR_TEXT)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "A4")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.add(dot_p, label_p, dot_f1, label_f1, dot_f2, label_f2, dot_a, label_a, dot_b, label_b)
        self.play(Create(line_pf1), Create(line_pf2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Show spheres and slant segment AB
        line_ab = Line(a_pos, b_pos, color=COLOR_AB, stroke_width=4)
        self.play(FadeIn(sphere_a), FadeIn(sphere_b))
        self.play(Create(line_ab))
        
        # Calculate target segments on AB for current P
        p_curr = dot_p.get_center()
        d1 = np.linalg.norm(p_curr - f1_pos)
        d2 = np.linalg.norm(p_curr - f2_pos)
        
        line_pa = Line(a_pos, a_pos + dir_ab * d1, color=COLOR_PF1, stroke_width=8)
        line_pb = Line(b_pos, b_pos - dir_ab * d2, color=COLOR_PF2, stroke_width=8)
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(line_pf1.copy(), line_pa),
            ReplacementTransform(line_pf2.copy(), line_pb),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Move P and show AB is constant
        # We need updaters for the segments
        p_tracker = ValueTracker(0.25)

        def update_p(m):
            m.move_to(ellipse_path.point_from_proportion(p_tracker.get_value() % 1.0))
        def update_label_p(m):
            m.next_to(dot_p, UP, buff=0.1)
        def update_pf1(m):
            m.set_points_as_corners([dot_p.get_center(), f1_pos])
        def update_pf2(m):
            m.set_points_as_corners([dot_p.get_center(), f2_pos])
        def update_pa(m):
            dist = np.linalg.norm(dot_p.get_center() - f1_pos)
            m.set_points_as_corners([a_pos, a_pos + dir_ab * dist])
        def update_pb(m):
            dist = np.linalg.norm(dot_p.get_center() - f2_pos)
            m.set_points_as_corners([b_pos, b_pos - dir_ab * dist])

        dot_p.add_updater(update_p)
        label_p.add_updater(update_label_p)
        line_pf1.add_updater(update_pf1)
        line_pf2.add_updater(update_pf2)
        line_pa.add_updater(update_pa)
        line_pb.add_updater(update_pb)

        self.play(p_tracker.animate.set_value(0.75), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(ellipse_path))
        self.play(p_tracker.animate.set_value(1.25), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        
        # Cleanup
        dot_p.clear_updaters()
        label_p.clear_updaters()
        line_pf1.clear_updaters()
        line_pf2.clear_updaters()
        line_pa.clear_updaters()
        line_pb.clear_updaters()
        
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(2)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial Setup
        title = "Universal Application: Parabolas and Hyperbolas"
        lines = [
            "Tilting the plane further changes the intersection's shape.",
            "Spheres still reveal the logic of parabolas and hyperbolas.",
            "Geometry and symmetry unite all conic sections."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        ELLIPSE_COLOR = "#00FF00"
        PARABOLA_COLOR = "#FFA500"
        HYPERBOLA_COLOR = "#FFC0CB"
        CONE_COLOR = BLUE_D

        # Right-side visualization center
        center_pt = (self.grid["A1"] + self.grid["F6"]) / 2
        v = center_pt # Vertex for the cone

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Representing an ellipse configuration
        self.lecture[0].set_color(ELLIPSE_COLOR)
        
        # Upper Cone Sides
        l1 = Line(v, v + 2.2 * rotate_vector(UP, 30*DEGREES), color=CONE_COLOR)
        l2 = Line(v, v + 2.2 * rotate_vector(UP, -30*DEGREES), color=CONE_COLOR)
        upper_cone = VGroup(l1, l2)
        
        # Cutting Plane (Ellipse state: horizontal)
        plane = Line(LEFT*1.2, RIGHT*1.2, color=ELLIPSE_COLOR)
        plane.move_to(v + UP * 1.2)
        
        # Dandelin Spheres for Ellipse
        s1 = Circle(radius=0.25, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.3).move_to(v + UP * 0.5)
        s2 = Circle(radius=0.55, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.3).move_to(v + UP * 1.8)
        
        self.play(Create(upper_cone), run_time=1)
        self.play(Create(plane), run_time=1)
        self.play(FadeIn(s1), FadeIn(s2), run_time=1)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Transition to Parabola: Tilt plane parallel to slant line l1
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(PARABOLA_COLOR)
        
        # Rotation angle for parabola: 60 degrees from horizontal
        self.play(
            plane.animate.set_color(PARABOLA_COLOR).rotate(60*DEGREES).move_to(v + UP*1.1 + RIGHT*0.4),
            s1.animate.scale(1.4).move_to(v + UP*0.85 + RIGHT*0.2),
            FadeOut(s2),
            run_time=2.5
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Transition to Hyperbola: Tilt plane further (vertical) and show double cone
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(HYPERBOLA_COLOR)
        
        # Lower Cone Sides
        l3 = Line(v, v + 2.2 * rotate_vector(DOWN, 30*DEGREES), color=CONE_COLOR)
        l4 = Line(v, v + 2.2 * rotate_vector(DOWN, -30*DEGREES), color=CONE_COLOR)
        lower_cone = VGroup(l3, l4)
        
        self.play(Create(lower_cone), run_time=1.5)
        
        # Rotate plane to vertical and position two spheres
        self.play(
            plane.animate.set_color(HYPERBOLA_COLOR).set_angle(90*DEGREES).move_to(v),
            s1.animate.scale(0.7).move_to(v + UP*0.7),
            run_time=2.5
        )
        # Bring back/adjust sphere 2 in the lower nappe
        s2.move_to(v + DOWN*0.7).scale(0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(s2), run_time=1)
        
        self.wait(3)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Ice Cream Cone Lemma", [
            "- Tangents from a point to a sphere are equal.",
            "- This is known as the \"Ice Cream Cone Lemma.\"",
            "- Distances from the vertex to the contact circle match."
        ])
        
        # Initial lecture colors - start dimmed for progressive highlight
        self.lecture.set_color(GRAY)
        
        # Visual Element Colors
        sphere_color = WHITE
        point_p_color = RED
        tangent_color = WHITE
        mark_color = WHITE
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # Create a circle representing the sphere (2D projection)
        sphere = Circle(radius=1.2, color=sphere_color)
        self.place_in_area(sphere, 'C3', 'E5')
        
        # Create point P outside the sphere
        p_dot = Dot(color=point_p_color)
        self.place_at_grid(p_dot, 'D1')
        p_label = MathTex("P", color=point_p_color).next_to(p_dot, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        # Geometry setup
        c = sphere.get_center()
        p = p_dot.get_center()
        r = sphere.radius
        cp_vec = p - c
        dist_cp = np.linalg.norm(cp_vec)
        
        # Calculate tangent points on the circle
        # In 2D, the angle of the tangent points relative to center is angle(P-C) +/- arccos(r/d)
        angle_cp = np.arctan2(cp_vec[1], cp_vec[0])
        angle_ct = np.arccos(r / dist_cp)
        
        t1_pos = c + r * np.array([np.cos(angle_cp + angle_ct), np.sin(angle_cp + angle_ct), 0])
        t2_pos = c + r * np.array([np.cos(angle_cp - angle_ct), np.sin(angle_cp - angle_ct), 0])
        
        l1 = Line(p, t1_pos, color=tangent_color)
        l2 = Line(p, t2_pos, color=tangent_color)
        
        self.play(Create(sphere), FadeIn(p_dot), Write(p_label))
        self.play(Create(l1), Create(l2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(RED))
        
        # Visualize the vertex of the "cone"
        self.play(Indicate(p_dot, color=RED), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # Flash both tangent segments to emphasize their equal lengths
        self.play(
            Flash(l1, color=WHITE, line_length=0.3, flash_radius=0.5),
            Flash(l2, color=WHITE, line_length=0.3, flash_radius=0.5)
        )
        
        # Equality markers (ticks)
        def create_tick(line):
            mid = line.get_center()
            vec = line.get_unit_vector()
            # Calculate a normal vector for the tick
            normal = np.array([-vec[1], vec[0], 0])
            return Line(mid - 0.12 * normal, mid + 0.12 * normal, color=mark_color, stroke_width=3)

        tick1 = create_tick(l1)
        tick2 = create_tick(l2)
        
        self.play(Create(tick1), Create(tick2))
        self.wait(2)

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE

        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup
        title_str = "The Constant Sum"
        lines_str = [
            "The sum PF1 + PF2 equals the total slant distance.",
            "This distance AB connects the two fixed circles.",
            "The length AB remains constant as point P moves.",
            "Thus, the sum of distances to foci is constant.",
            "The Dandelin spheres prove this curve is an ellipse."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_str, lines_str)

        # Colors
        COLOR_PF1 = "#0000FF" # Blue
        COLOR_PF2 = "#FF4500" # Orange-red
        COLOR_AB = "#00FF00"  # Green
        COLOR_TEXT = "#FFFFFF"

        # Assets
        sphere_asset_path = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg"

        # Points
        f1_pos = self.grid["D2"] + RIGHT * 0.2
        f2_pos = self.grid["D5"] + LEFT * 0.2
        a_pos = self.grid["C3"]
        b_pos = self.grid["E5"]
        
        # Fixed distance AB length
        ab_len = np.linalg.norm(b_pos - a_pos)
        
        # P's path - Ellipse logic
        # Sum of distances to foci = constant = ab_len
        center_ellipse = (f1_pos + f2_pos) / 2
        c_dist = np.linalg.norm(f1_pos - center_ellipse)
        a_semi = ab_len / 2
        b_semi = np.sqrt(max(a_semi**2 - c_dist**2, 0.1)) # semi-minor axis
        
        ellipse_path = Ellipse(width=2*a_semi, height=2*b_semi, color=GRAY, stroke_opacity=0.3).move_to(center_ellipse)
        
        # Initial P (proportion 0.25 for a good starting angle)
        dot_p = Dot(ellipse_path.point_from_proportion(0.25), color=WHITE)
        label_p = Text("P", font_size=18).next_to(dot_p, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        dot_f1 = Dot(f1_pos, color=COLOR_PF1)
        label_f1 = Text("F1", font_size=18, color=COLOR_PF1).next_to(dot_f1, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        dot_f2 = Dot(f2_pos, color=COLOR_PF2)
        label_f2 = Text("F2", font_size=18, color=COLOR_PF2).next_to(dot_f2, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        dot_a = Dot(a_pos, color=COLOR_PF1)
        label_a = Text("A", font_size=18, color=COLOR_PF1).next_to(dot_a, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        dot_b = Dot(b_pos, color=COLOR_PF2)
        label_b = Text("B", font_size=18, color=COLOR_PF2).next_to(dot_b, RIGHT, buff=0.1)

        # Spheres at A and B
        sphere_a = SVGMobject(sphere_asset_path).scale(0.4).move_to(a_pos + UP*0.4)
        sphere_b = SVGMobject(sphere_asset_path).scale(0.6).move_to(b_pos + DOWN*0.6)

        # Segments
        line_pf1 = Line(dot_p.get_center(), f1_pos, color=COLOR_PF1)
        line_pf2 = Line(dot_p.get_center(), f2_pos, color=COLOR_PF2)
        
        # Components of AB segment
        dir_ab = (b_pos - a_pos) / ab_len
        
        # Formula using Text to avoid LaTeX issues
        formula = Text("PF1 + PF2 = AB", font_size=24, color=COLOR_TEXT)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "A4")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.add(dot_p, label_p, dot_f1, label_f1, dot_f2, label_f2, dot_a, label_a, dot_b, label_b)
        self.play(Create(line_pf1), Create(line_pf2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Show spheres and slant segment AB
        line_ab = Line(a_pos, b_pos, color=COLOR_AB, stroke_width=4)
        self.play(FadeIn(sphere_a), FadeIn(sphere_b))
        self.play(Create(line_ab))
        
        # Calculate target segments on AB for current P
        p_curr = dot_p.get_center()
        d1 = np.linalg.norm(p_curr - f1_pos)
        d2 = np.linalg.norm(p_curr - f2_pos)
        
        line_pa = Line(a_pos, a_pos + dir_ab * d1, color=COLOR_PF1, stroke_width=8)
        line_pb = Line(b_pos, b_pos - dir_ab * d2, color=COLOR_PF2, stroke_width=8)
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(line_pf1.copy(), line_pa),
            ReplacementTransform(line_pf2.copy(), line_pb),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Move P and show AB is constant
        # We need updaters for the segments
        p_tracker = ValueTracker(0.25)

        def update_p(m):
            m.move_to(ellipse_path.point_from_proportion(p_tracker.get_value() % 1.0))
        def update_label_p(m):
            m.next_to(dot_p, UP, buff=0.1)
        def update_pf1(m):
            m.set_points_as_corners([dot_p.get_center(), f1_pos])
        def update_pf2(m):
            m.set_points_as_corners([dot_p.get_center(), f2_pos])
        def update_pa(m):
            dist = np.linalg.norm(dot_p.get_center() - f1_pos)
            m.set_points_as_corners([a_pos, a_pos + dir_ab * dist])
        def update_pb(m):
            dist = np.linalg.norm(dot_p.get_center() - f2_pos)
            m.set_points_as_corners([b_pos, b_pos - dir_ab * dist])

        dot_p.add_updater(update_p)
        label_p.add_updater(update_label_p)
        line_pf1.add_updater(update_pf1)
        line_pf2.add_updater(update_pf2)
        line_pa.add_updater(update_pa)
        line_pb.add_updater(update_pb)

        self.play(p_tracker.animate.set_value(0.75), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(ellipse_path))
        self.play(p_tracker.animate.set_value(1.25), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        
        # Cleanup
        dot_p.clear_updaters()
        label_p.clear_updaters()
        line_pf1.clear_updaters()
        line_pf2.clear_updaters()
        line_pa.clear_updaters()
        line_pb.clear_updaters()

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Section title and lecture lines
        title_text = "The Visual Proof: Linking Segments"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Pick any point P on the elliptical slice.",
            "Connect P to the foci F1 and F2.",
            "PF1 equals the distance to the upper contact circle.",
            "PF2 equals the distance to the lower contact circle.",
            "These segments align along the cone's slant height."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_P = "#FF0000"
        COLOR_BLUE = "#0000FF"
        COLOR_ORANGE = "#FF4500"
        COLOR_CONE = GREY_C
        COLOR_SPHERE = GREY_B
        COLOR_PLANE = "#FFFFE0" # Light Yellow

        # Grid references
        g = self.grid

        # Pre-calculated geometry for visual proof consistency
        # P is the point on the ellipse
        # F1, F2 are the foci
        # A, B are points on the upper/lower contact circles along the slant height through P
        # Distances: PF1 = PA, PF2 = PB
        # Collinearity: A, P, B are on a straight line (the slant height)
        
        # Grid Coordinates (Indices start at 1):
        # P: D4 (x=1.5+3=4.5, y=2.2-3=-0.8)
        # F1: C2 (x=1.5+1=2.5, y=2.2-2=0.2) -> dist = sqrt(2^2+1^2) = sqrt(5)
        # A: B3 (x=1.5+2=3.5, y=2.2-1=1.2) -> dist = sqrt(1^2+2^2) = sqrt(5)
        # F2: E6 (x=1.5+5=6.5, y=2.2-4=-1.8) -> dist = sqrt(2^2+1^2) = sqrt(5)
        # B: F5 (x=1.5+4=5.5, y=2.2-5=-2.8) -> dist = sqrt(1^2+2^2) = sqrt(5)
        # Apex: (x=3.0, y=2.2) [Midpoint of A2 and A3]

        f1_pos = g["C2"]
        f2_pos = g["E6"]
        a_pos = g["B3"]
        b_pos = g["F5"]

        # "Pick any point P on the elliptical slice."
        # Display the cone, plane, and spheres with a red point P (#FF0000) on the ellipse.
        
        # Cone sides

        slant_r = Line(apex_pos, g["F6"], color=COLOR_CONE)
        
        # Spheres
        sphere1 = Circle(radius=0.7, color=COLOR_SPHERE, stroke_opacity=0.8).set_fill(COLOR_SPHERE, opacity=0.3)

        # Point P

        label_p = MathTex("P", color=COLOR_P, font_size=24).next_to(dot_p, UP, buff=0.1)

        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(
            Create(slant_l), Create(slant_r),
            FadeIn(sphere1), FadeIn(sphere2),

            FadeIn(dot_p), Write(label_p),

        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

        label_f1 = MathTex("F_1", color=WHITE, font_size=24).next_to(dot_f1, DL, buff=0.1)

        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(
            FadeIn(dot_f1), Write(label_f1),
            FadeIn(dot_f2), Write(label_f2),
            Create(seg_pf1), Create(seg_pf2),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "PF1 equals the distance to the upper contact circle."
        dot_a = Dot(a_pos, color=COLOR_BLUE)
        label_a = MathTex("A", color=COLOR_BLUE, font_size=24).next_to(dot_a, UR, buff=0.1)
        seg_pa = Line(p_pos, a_pos, color=COLOR_BLUE)

        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(
            FadeIn(dot_a), Write(label_a),
            Create(seg_pa)
        )
        # Highlight equality visually
        self.play(seg_pf1.animate.set_stroke(width=8), seg_pa.animate.set_stroke(width=8), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(seg_pf1.animate.set_stroke(width=4), seg_pa.animate.set_stroke(width=4), run_time=0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "PF2 equals the distance to the lower contact circle."
        dot_b = Dot(b_pos, color=COLOR_ORANGE)

        seg_pb = Line(p_pos, b_pos, color=COLOR_ORANGE)

        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(
            FadeIn(dot_b), Write(label_b),
            Create(seg_pb)

        self.play(seg_pf2.animate.set_stroke(width=4), seg_pb.animate.set_stroke(width=4), run_time=0.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "These segments align along the cone's slant height."
        # Highlight the straight line AB through P
        seg_ab = Line(a_pos, b_pos, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(
            Create(seg_ab),
            seg_pa.animate.set_color(YELLOW),

            "The sum PF1 + PF2 equals the total slant distance.",
            "This distance AB connects the two fixed circles.",
            "The length AB remains constant as point P moves.",
            "Thus, the sum of distances to foci is constant.",
            "The Dandelin spheres prove this curve is an ellipse."

        line_pf2 = Line(dot_p.get_center(), f2_pos, color=COLOR_PF2)

        dir_ab = (b_pos - a_pos) / ab_len

        def update_pf2(m):

        def update_pb(m):

        line_pf1.add_updater(update_pf1)
        line_pf2.add_updater(update_pf2)
        line_pa.add_updater(update_pa)
        line_pb.add_updater(update_pb)

        self.lecture[3].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)

        self.lecture[4].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)

        self.play(p_tracker.animate.set_value(1.25), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)

        label_p.clear_updaters()
        line_pf1.clear_updaters()
        line_pf2.clear_updaters()

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Section title and lecture lines
        title_text = "The Visual Proof: Linking Segments"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Pick any point P on the elliptical slice.",
            "Connect P to the foci F1 and F2.",
            "PF1 equals the distance to the upper contact circle.",
            "PF2 equals the distance to the lower contact circle.",
            "These segments align along the cone's slant height."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Assets paths
        ASSET_CONE = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cone.svg"
        ASSET_SPHERE = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg"

        # Colors
        COLOR_P = "#FF0000"
        COLOR_BLUE = "#0000FF"
        COLOR_ORANGE = "#FF4500"
        COLOR_PLANE = "#FFFFE0"
        
        # Grid references
        g = self.grid

        # Geometrically consistent positions (Calculated to ensure PA=PF1 and PB=PF2)
        # and A, P, B are collinear on the slant height.
        p_pos = g["D5"]
        a_pos = g["B4"]
        b_pos = g["F6"]
        f1_pos = g["C3"]
        f2_pos = g["F4"]

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Pick any point P on the elliptical slice."
        # Display the cone, plane, and spheres with a red point P (#FF0000) on the ellipse.
        
        # Cone SVG
        cone_svg = SVGMobject(ASSET_CONE, color=GREY_C, fill_opacity=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(cone_svg, "A3", "F6", scale_factor=2.5)
        
        # Spheres SVG (Addressing issues 36, 37, 42)
        sphere1 = SVGMobject(ASSET_SPHERE, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(sphere1, 'A4', 'B5', scale_factor=0.7)
        
        sphere2 = SVGMobject(ASSET_SPHERE, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(sphere2, 'D4', 'F5', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Plane line (as slice)
        plane_line = Line(g["C3"], g["F6"], color=COLOR_PLANE, stroke_width=2)
        
        # Point P
        dot_p = Dot(p_pos, color=COLOR_P)
        label_p = MathTex("P", color=COLOR_P, font_size=24).next_to(dot_p, RIGHT, buff=0.1)

        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(
            FadeIn(cone_svg),
            FadeIn(sphere1), FadeIn(sphere2),
            Create(plane_line),
            FadeIn(dot_p), Write(label_p),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Connect P to the foci F1 and F2."
        dot_f1 = Dot(f1_pos, color=WHITE)
        label_f1 = MathTex("F_1", color=WHITE, font_size=24).next_to(dot_f1, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        dot_f2 = Dot(f2_pos, color=WHITE)
        label_f2 = MathTex("F_2", color=WHITE, font_size=24).next_to(dot_f2, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        seg_pf1 = Line(p_pos, f1_pos, color=COLOR_BLUE)
        seg_pf2 = Line(p_pos, f2_pos, color=COLOR_ORANGE)

        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(
            FadeIn(dot_f1), Write(label_f1),
            FadeIn(dot_f2), Write(label_f2),
            Create(seg_pf1), Create(seg_pf2),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "PF1 equals the distance to the upper contact circle."
        dot_a = Dot(a_pos, color=COLOR_BLUE)
        label_a = MathTex("A", color=COLOR_BLUE, font_size=24).next_to(dot_a, UP, buff=0.1)
        seg_pa = Line(p_pos, a_pos, color=COLOR_BLUE)

        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(
            FadeIn(dot_a), Write(label_a),
            Create(seg_pa)
        )
        # Highlight equality visually
        self.play(seg_pf1.animate.set_stroke(width=8), seg_pa.animate.set_stroke(width=8), run_time=0.5)

        lines_str = [
            "The sum PF1 + PF2 equals the total slant distance.",
            "This distance AB connects the two fixed circles.",
            "The length AB remains constant as point P moves.",
            "Thus, the sum of distances to foci is constant.",

        dot_a = Dot(a_pos, color=COLOR_PF1)
        label_a = Text("A", font_size=18, color=COLOR_PF1).next_to(dot_a, LEFT, buff=0.1)

        sphere_b = SVGMobject(sphere_asset_path).scale(0.6).move_to(b_pos + DOWN*0.6)

        line_pf2 = Line(dot_p.get_center(), f2_pos, color=COLOR_PF2)

        self.lecture[1].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)

        self.play(FadeIn(sphere_a), FadeIn(sphere_b))

        p_curr = dot_p.get_center()
        d1 = np.linalg.norm(p_curr - f1_pos)

            m.move_to(ellipse_path.point_from_proportion(p_tracker.get_value() % 1.0))
        def update_label_p(m):
            m.next_to(dot_p, UP, buff=0.1)
        def update_pf1(m):
            m.set_points_as_corners([dot_p.get_center(), f1_pos])
        def update_pf2(m):
            m.set_points_as_corners([dot_p.get_center(), f2_pos])
        def update_pa(m):
            dist = np.linalg.norm(dot_p.get_center() - f1_pos)
            m.set_points_as_corners([a_pos, a_pos + dir_ab * dist])
        def update_pb(m):
            dist = np.linalg.norm(dot_p.get_center() - f2_pos)
            m.set_points_as_corners([b_pos, b_pos - dir_ab * dist])

        label_p.add_updater(update_label_p)
        line_pf1.add_updater(update_pf1)
        line_pf2.add_updater(update_pf2)
        line_pa.add_updater(update_pa)
        line_pb.add_updater(update_pb)

        self.wait(1)

        self.lecture[3].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        self.play(Create(ellipse_path))
        self.play(p_tracker.animate.set_value(1.25), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        
        # Cleanup
        dot_p.clear_updaters()
        label_p.clear_updaters()
        line_pf1.clear_updaters()
        line_pf2.clear_updaters()
        line_pa.clear_updaters()
        line_pb.clear_updaters()

        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        # Setup
        title_str = "The Constant Sum"

            "The Dandelin spheres prove this curve is an ellipse."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_str, lines_str)

        # Colors
        COLOR_PF1 = "#0000FF" # Blue
